tool_input.command:
git add internal/mission/store.go internal/mission/store_test.go && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(mission): DisclaimDelegation takes the delegation lock the refusal-closers already hold (P1, qodo #7)

Review finding P1 (qodo #7, full-branch review of PR #509,
m-2026-09-08-004 round 3) -- ethos-lj4k's exact class, previously fixed
on this same bead for Abandon vs a concurrent dispatch, found again for
DisclaimDelegation vs the refusal-close paths
(pretooluse_dispatch.go's closeDelegationAborted, subagent_start.go's
closeSkeletonOnHashRefusal).

Verified before fixing: closeDelegationAborted runs inside dispatchTierB
while it holds the SHARED AcquireMissionLock, which already excludes
DisclaimDelegation's EXCLUSIVE AcquireMissionLockExclusive (a normal
reader-writer pair) -- that specific pairing was never actually racy.
closeSkeletonOnHashRefusal is different: it runs from an entirely
separate SubagentStart process invocation that never touches the
mission lock at all, so nothing excluded it from loading record.yaml,
writing its own verdict:aborted mutation from a stale pre-disclaim
copy, and silently reverting DisclaimedAt/DisclaimedReason -- a
delegation that looked disclaimed would go back to blocking Abandon
with no error and no signal why.

DisclaimDelegation now also acquires AcquireDelegationLock for the
specific delegation ID, nested inside its existing mission-exclusive
lock. Neither refusal-close path ever escalates from
AcquireDelegationLock to AcquireMissionLockExclusive, so this nesting
is one-directional and introduces no new deadlock risk -- verified by
running the full mission package suite under -race after the change.

TestStore_DisclaimDelegation_SerializesWithDelegationLockHolder proves
actual exclusion, not a race that happens to resolve correctly: a
goroutine holding the same per-delegation lock must block
DisclaimDelegation until it releases. Confirmed failing against pre-fix
code (DisclaimDelegation completed immediately while the lock was held).
EOF
)"
